A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VQ-SGen, with matching authors, core architecture, and CreativeSketch experiments. The main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark comparisons, component and codebook ablations, qualitative generation experiments, and a 50-participant user study.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds conditional-generation demonstrations, location-codebook experiments, QuickDraw reconstruction examples, and a Diffsketcher comparison.

M1.justification: The core VQ representation, losses, and cascaded generator remain unchanged. Section 5 adds limited conditioning adaptations: class-conditioned generation removes the label Transformer and replaces STR with a class-index token, while text-conditioned generation replaces STR with a pretrained CLIP text embedding.

E1.justification: V2 adds class-conditioned generation on a 20-class QuickDraw subset, text-conditioned generation using Creative Birds/Creatures descriptions, and reconstruction of unseen QuickDraw sketches. These substantially extend the evaluated populations and input conditions. QuickDraw previously appeared only as the evaluation model's training-data source; the earlier initial-stroke conditional task remains as sketch completion.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SketchKnitter, DoodlerGAN, and DoodleFormer, and the completion comparison retains DoodlerGAN and DoodleFormer. V2 adds Diffsketcher as an evaluated comparator for text-conditioned generation in Appendix D and Figure A3, including qualitative examples and a runtime comparison.

E3.justification: The retained benchmark and user-study protocols remain stable. Added experiments introduce generator-only retraining for QuickDraw, reconstruction without fine-tuning, bounding-box mean IoU for location-codebook evaluation, and specified Diffsketcher prompt templates. Appendix B also changes the reported generator learning rate from v1's appendix value of 10^-4 to 10^-5, matching v1's main text; this correction does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds separate location-codebook sensitivity experiments measuring reconstruction and generation quality (Table A1, Figure A2), plus cross-dataset reconstruction tests without fine-tuning (Figure A6). Appendix D also reports qualitative prompt/seed sensitivity checks. The existing component ablations, shape-codebook sweep, UMAP analysis, interpolation, and failure cases remain; interpolation and failures are relocated.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly reports testing different random seeds for Diffsketcher, without specifying their identities or number. Neither version provides benchmark confidence intervals or formal significance tests. This is additional seed information, with no documented increase in repeated runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 and Figure 6 retain their results, including VQ-SGen FIDs of 15.78 and 17.61. V2 adds location-codebook results, including final mean IoUs of 0.963 and 0.957, class/text generation examples, and QuickDraw reconstruction findings. Appendix D newly reports runtimes of 0.86 seconds versus Diffsketcher's 153 seconds, although matched timing conditions are insufficiently documented.

T1.justification: The stroke-triplet definition, nearest-code assignment, reconstruction and VQ losses, autoregressive factorization, and generation objective are unchanged. The previously unnumbered reconstruction equation receives a number. No new formal assumptions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about stroke-level VQ generation and superior CreativeSketch performance remain. The abstract replaces the advertised semantic-aware stroke-editing application with explicit text/class-conditioned generation and sketch completion, and expressly scopes its performance claim to CreativeSketch.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands applicability and mechanism interpretations: label removal supports use without stroke annotations, QuickDraw reconstruction is interpreted as transferable shape-prior learning, and Diffsketcher's creative limitations are attributed to realistic-image pretraining. Appendix C adds discussion of codebook quality versus computational cost. The earlier nonoptimal-hyperparameter and hard-cropping limitations remain in Appendix E.

D1.justification: V2 newly clarifies default drawing order and translation without rescaling, and documents class-token conditioning, CLIP text conditioning, generator-only QuickDraw retraining, and comparison prompts. It reconciles the conflicting generator learning-rate disclosures. Existing hardware, batch sizes, training times, architecture details, augmentation, and sampling information are largely retained or relocated; the code-release promise is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 now explicitly credits ContextSeg's stroke entities and SketchXAI's shape/location decomposition, positioning VQ-SGen as adopting those concepts and adding discrete representations for generation. V2 also develops a substantive creativity-versus-realism comparison with Diffsketcher, adds relevant conditioning and sketch-literature citations, and removes the 3D ShapeFormer example. This changes positioning beyond citation expansion alone.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the opening motivation and related-work discussion, reorganizes Section 5 around code-space exploration and three applications, and consolidates training information in the supplement. Interpolation and limitations move out of the main discussion, while the supplement is reorganized from four numbered sections into sections A-F. Much of the core method prose remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 7 becomes a three-panel application display, reducing the earlier 16 completion examples to four alongside new class/text examples. Figure 8's interpolation panel moves to Figure A4. V2 adds Table A1 and Figures A2, A3, and A6, relocates existing supplementary figures, and rearranges the main comparison and reconstruction figures onto one page.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for the representation through separate location-codebook measurements, provides initial evidence for additional applications and transfer, improves attribution to ContextSeg and SketchXAI, and resolves the learning-rate inconsistency. These are concrete gains in support and reproducibility. Their overall impact is limited because the new transfer and text-generation claims rely mainly on selected qualitative examples, the timing comparison lacks matched protocol details, and the established benchmark and user-study evidence is unchanged.
